title: DragonSpeed wins Spa as WRT's one-off nearly steals it
dek: Pole-sitter Nicolas Lapierre took DragonSpeed's first ELMS win in the Oreca #21, passing the fuel-saving WRT Ligier of Laurens Vanthoor with about half an hour left after two long Safety Cars reshuffled the order.

chapters.title: Title race on a bonus date
text: The 4 Hours of Spa-Francorchamps on 25 September 2016 was the penultimate round of the European Le Mans Series and the series' first race at the Belgian circuit since 2011, with the Estoril finale to follow in October. In LMP2, Thiriet by TDS Racing arrived as championship leader after winning the previous three races, and the #46 Oreca 05 of Pierre Thiriet, Mathias Beche and Ryo Hirakawa was reunited: Hirakawa was back after missing Le Castellet for the Suzuka 1000km, where Mike Conway had stood in. G-Drive Racing, with its Gibson-powered #38, was the title-contending team chasing the Frenchmen.

The class grew to 13 cars with a surprise newcomer. Team WRT, the Blancpain GT Series regulars, rented the ex-So24! Ligier JS P2 Judd, numbered #47, for Laurens Vanthoor, his younger brother Dries and former Formula 1 driver Will Stevens. Team boss Vincent Vosse called it a one-off and a test of whether a full LMP2 programme made sense for 2017. There were other changes: Vitaly Petrov joined Stefano Coletti and Andreas Wirth in the SMP Racing BR 01, Michael Munemann took over the Algarve Pro Ligier #25 from Gianluca Roda, and Murphy Prototypes ran a reshuffled Findlay, Bonifacio and Doyle line-up in its Oreca 03R.

On track, DragonSpeed set the tone. Nicolas Lapierre topped Friday's opening practice in the Oreca #21 by 0.093 seconds from the SMP car, with Olivier Pla's Krohn Ligier third and Beche fourth, and G-Drive was only 11th. Lapierre was fastest again on Saturday morning, nearly a second quicker, with the Eurasia Oreca #33 of Tristan Gommendy second. That session ended early with a red flag when Wirth went off, and the debutant WRT car had a heavy shunt for Laurens Vanthoor, who reported a stuck throttle. The team rebuilt the car around a new tub overnight.

chapters.title: Lapierre dominates, WRT recovers to eighth
text: Lapierre completed a clean sweep of the pre-race sessions by taking pole with a 2:06.603, the second pole of the year for DragonSpeed. His margin over championship leader Beche was 0.445 seconds, as the Thiriet Oreca 05 produced a late effort that fell short of the Frenchman's time. Harry Tincknell put the G-Drive Gibson third on 2:07.214, with Gommendy fourth for Eurasia, so the top four were covered by 0.7 seconds.

Andrea Pizzitola and Nathanael Berthon followed in fifth and sixth in the Algarve Pro and Greaves Ligiers, separated by just 0.011 seconds, with Coletti seventh in the SMP car. The repaired WRT Ligier qualified eighth for Vanthoor on 2:08.253, with Paul Loup Chatin's Panis Barthez Ligier ninth. Murphy, Pegasus and Krohn filled the next three places, while the IDEC Sport Ligier #28 started 13th after an engine failure in the second practice session left Dimitri Enjalbert with a lap of 2:19.616, more than 12 seconds off the pole time.

chapters.title: Wheel off, Full Course Yellows and the first stops
text: The 2 p.m. start was clean for Lapierre but cautious for Beche's team-mate Thiriet, who started the #46 and quickly lost two places to the G-Drive Gibson and the Eurasia Oreca. Eurasia's race was over almost at once: the #33 lost a rear wheel and stopped on track during the first lap, which brought out a short Full Course Yellow. After the restart Lapierre consolidated his lead from the #38 and the Greaves Ligier #41.

On lap 10 contact between the Krohn Racing Ligier #40 and a GTE Ferrari triggered a second Full Course Yellow. When the race resumed, Lapierre stretched the gap to the #46 and the SMP car, and the leading cars made their first stops around lap 20. That handed the lead to the #38 and the WRT Ligier, who stopped about ten laps later. Thiriet's Oreca inherited the lead as the stops cycled through.

chapters.title: Two Safety Cars turn the order upside down
text: The race turned at Bruxelles. On lap 37 Garry Findlay put the Murphy Oreca 03R into the barriers, and the Safety Car came out. The SMP car pitted at once, and Thiriet used the interruption to hand over to Hirakawa. G-Drive had been running a staggered pit strategy, and when the field was released Simon Dolan's Gibson was in front. Soon after the halfway mark, and after only a few green-flag laps, Remy Striebig crashed the Pegasus Morgan at the same corner and the race went back under a long Safety Car period. By then the pole-sitting DragonSpeed was fourth and the TDS car sixth.

Strategy decided the next phase. Most leaders stayed out under the Safety Car, but WRT brought the #47 in, and several others, including the DragonSpeed, TDS and G-Drive cars, pitted just as the Safety Car pulled in and the track went green, losing precious time. WRT came out in front, ahead of the DragonSpeed Oreca and three close rivals: the IDEC Ligier #28, the Algarve Pro Ligier #25 and the SMP BR 01. The IDEC car drifted back, and the SMP car lost time with a headlight repair. By the end of the neutralised periods, the Safety Cars and Full Course Yellows had taken almost an hour out of the race.

chapters.title: Lapierre hunts down the leader
text: Around 50 minutes from the finish Laurens Vanthoor took the Ligier back from his brother Dries and led again, with 48 seconds in hand over the TDS Oreca. It was a precarious lead: the WRT car was saving fuel and lapping more than two seconds a lap slower than Lapierre, who had started the race and was now back in the DragonSpeed Oreca for the last stint. The fight for the lead was played out on a track that was partly wet.

Lapierre closed the gap quickly and, with a little over 30 minutes left, passed Vanthoor at Les Combes. The WRT driver had no radio contact with the pits for the last stint and drove conservatively, knowing a last splash of fuel might be needed. Behind them Beche and Pizzitola fought for third until the Algarve Pro Ligier ended in the gravel trap at Campus Corner in the last five minutes, which left Beche to take the chequered flag in third place.

chapters.title: DragonSpeed's first win, WRT second on its debut
text: The race ended under a Full Course Yellow while the Algarve Pro car was recovered, after 4:01:13 of racing. Lapierre, Ben Hanley and Henrik Hedman won in the #21 Oreca 05 after 96 laps from pole, completing the team's perfect weekend of fastest in both practices, pole and victory. WRT finished second on the lead lap on its first appearance in the series, with Vanthoor, Stevens and Dries Vanthoor sharing the car. Thiriet by TDS took third, 39.967 seconds behind the winner, and the quickest lap of the race was Beche's 2:08.796.

Greaves Motorsport's Ligier #41 of Memo Rojas, Julien Canal and Berthon was fourth, and G-Drive's Gibson, which had led the race at half distance, ended fifth for Dolan, Tincknell and Giedo van der Garde after the late-stop mistake. SMP, Panis Barthez and IDEC were all one lap down in sixth to eighth, and the stricken Algarve Pro car was classified ninth, two laps behind. Krohn Racing was the only other classified LMP2 car, 30th overall and nine laps down.

chapters.title: A first win for Elton Julian's team
text: For DragonSpeed it was a breakthrough. The win was the American team's first in the European Le Mans Series, in its maiden year with the Oreca 05. Team owner Elton Julian said he planned to upgrade Hedman's existing car to Oreca 07 specification and add a second new one for 2017, keeping the ELMS as the focus, and he was evaluating a one-car entry at the Rolex 24 at Daytona with the new car, a decision due in December. He also said that if the team went, it would go to try to win.

For Team WRT it was a remarkable debut, and Vosse had already said the outcome would shape any full-time 2017 LMP2 campaign. Laurens Vanthoor said he had lost radio contact with the pits for his last stint and drove conservatively, knowing he would probably need a final splash of fuel. The race was also a lesson in Safety Car timing: the G-Drive, TDS and SMP crews that pitted just as the track went green dropped down the order, while WRT, which had stopped earlier, gained the lead.

In the title fight, the third place extended the points lead of Thiriet by TDS over G-Drive Racing, but fifth place left G-Drive alive, and the LMP2 championship goes to the Estoril finale on 23 October. The team's manager, Xavier Combet, spoke of a possible dual ELMS and WEC campaign in 2017, with an upgraded Oreca 05 alongside a new car. Elsewhere the paddock was already looking forward: the series announced a 2017 calendar with Monza and Portimao replacing Imola and Estoril, and said that 2017-specification LMP2 cars would race for the overall win, while current-generation cars would get their own podium but no title.

Several LMP2 programmes spent the weekend planning for next season. Pegasus Racing, whose Morgan will not be eligible for the top LMP2 class in 2017, was undecided, and Julien Schell mentioned LMP3 as a fall-back. IDEC Sport confirmed the purchase of a Ligier JS P217 for delivery in February, while Graff said it would stay in the ELMS with a new Oreca 07 rather than move to the WEC, with an eye on an entry for the Le Mans 24 Hours.

facts.v: The Oreca 05 #21 of Hedman, Lapierre and Hanley converted pole into the American team's first European Le Mans Series victory.
